items.q: You edited app.py and ran git commit -m "fix" but git says "nothing to commit". What did you forget?
options: git push before committing
git add app.py to stage the change
git init in the folder again
git checkout main first
items.explain: A commit only records staged changes; git add moves your edit from the working tree into the staging area.

items.q:
During git merge feature, git stops and app.py contains this. What must you do?

<<<<<<< HEAD
rate = 0.18
=======
rate = 0.12
>>>>>>> feature
options: Run git merge --continue and git chooses the newer line
Edit to keep the right line, remove markers, git add, commit
Delete the file and run git pull
Run git rebase to remove the markers automatically
items.explain: Git cannot decide between two edits to the same lines; you resolve by hand, then stage and commit to finish the merge.

items.q: Your last commit has a typo in its message and you have not pushed it yet. Which command fixes the message?
options: git commit --amend
git revert HEAD
git reset --hard HEAD~1
git rebase main
items.explain: --amend rewrites the most recent commit in place; revert makes a new commit and reset --hard throws the commit away.

items.q: You accidentally committed .env with a secret and pushed it to a public repo. Which is the correct set of actions?
options: Add .env to .gitignore and push; the file disappears from history
Rotate the secret, remove the file, ignore it, rewrite history
Delete the repo's main branch and recreate it
Run git rm --cached .env only; the old commit is safe
items.explain: Anything pushed is already exposed, so the secret must be rotated first; .gitignore only stops future tracking, it does not touch history.

items.q: logs/debug.log is already tracked by git. You add "logs/" to .gitignore. What happens on the next commit?
options: The file is removed from the repo automatically
Changes to debug.log are still tracked until you git rm --cached it
Git errors because an ignored file is tracked
The file is kept but marked read-only
items.explain: .gitignore only affects untracked files; a file already in the index keeps being tracked until you remove it from the index.

items.q: main has commits A-B. You branched feature at B and made C-D. Meanwhile main got E. After git rebase main on feature, what does feature look like?
options: A-B-E-C'-D'
A-B-C-D-E
A-B-E-M (one merge commit M)
A-B-C-D (E is not included)
items.explain: Rebase replays your commits on top of the new main tip, creating new commits C' and D' and a straight-line history.

options: Downloads new commits only, without changing your branch
Fetches from the remote and merges (or rebases) into your current branch
Uploads your commits to the remote
Creates a pull request on GitHub
items.explain: pull is fetch plus merge (or rebase, if configured); a plain fetch never changes your working branch.

items.q: You committed a bug 3 commits ago on main, which is already pushed and used by teammates. Which command undoes that change safely?
options: git reset --hard HEAD~3 then git push --force
git revert <bad_commit_sha>
git checkout HEAD~3 -- .
git rebase -i HEAD~3 and drop the commit, then push
items.explain: revert adds a new commit that reverses the change, keeping shared history intact; rewriting pushed history breaks everyone else's clones.

items.q: You pushed a branch and opened a pull request. The reviewer asks for one more change. What is the normal way to update the PR?
options: Close the PR and open a new one from a fresh branch
Commit on the same branch and push; the PR updates
Edit the file in the PR description
Merge main into the PR from the GitHub UI
items.explain: A pull request tracks a branch, so every new push to that branch appears in the same PR.

items.q: You changed config.py, have not staged it, and want to throw the change away and get the last committed version back. Which command?
options: git restore config.py
git rm config.py
git stash pop
git commit config.py
items.explain: restore (or the older checkout -- file) overwrites the working copy with the version in the index or last commit.

items.q:
git status shows:

On branch main
Your branch is ahead of 'origin/main' by 2 commits.
nothing to commit, working tree clean

What is true?
options: Two commits on the remote are missing locally
You have 2 local commits that are not yet pushed
Two files are staged but not committed
The remote branch was deleted
items.explain: "Ahead by 2" means your local main has two commits the remote does not; git push sends them.
